result.title: Chain of Faith: Policy-Internal Rewards for Reasoning Reliance
result.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) explanations can sound plausible while having little influence on a model's final answer. We study four rewards that use the policy's own signals to encourage reliance on generated reasoning: gradient sensitivity, confidence gaps, progressive confidence gains, and reasoning--prompt swaps. We add each reward to group relative policy optimization (GRPO) and evaluate two small instruction-tuned models on GSM8K and StrategyQA using reasoning edits, paraphrases, and prompt hints. Several configurations increase answer reliance to reasoning edits, while effects on accuracy and paraphrase robustness vary. We also observe answer copying at a high reward weight and high reliance in decomposition settings with poor task accuracy. The study compares practical objectives for reasoning reliance, confirms the trade-off between reliance and performance, and proposes four lightweight rewards that can improve reasoning reliance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出四种基于策略自身信号的轻量奖励（梯度敏感度、置信度差、渐进置信增益、推理—提示互换），加入 GRPO 训练两个小型指令模型，并在 GSM8K 与 StrategyQA 上用推理编辑、复述和提示线索检验答案是否真正依赖所生成的 CoT。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「答案是否真正使用推理内容」的依赖度量与奖励监督思路，可供核查能否迁移到判断 VLM 答案是否使用 latent 视觉推理内容，并涉及依赖性与任务性能的权衡；但对象是纯文本 CoT，非视觉。
